sources.entry: 📖 Incident Metrics in SRE, Štěpán Davidovič, Google

summary.title: Incident Metrics in SRE: Critically Evaluating MTTR and Friends
summary.one_liner: MTTR-style incident metrics are poorly suited to judging reliability improvements, as shown by Monte Carlo simulation on real public incident-duration data, and the report suggests alternatives.
takeaways: MTTR and MTTM are often used to judge reliability improvements, but they can mislead in typical SRE incident settings.
Incident durations are positively skewed with huge variance, so a mean-based metric is unstable across samples.
A Monte Carlo simulation of parallel 'universes' shows that random chance alone can make MTTR appear to improve or worsen substantially.
Larger incident counts reduce the variance of the observed mean, but the report argues for tailoring metrics to the specific question instead of seeking one silver bullet.
summary.summary: This O'Reilly report by Google SRE Štěpán Davidovič critically examines MTTR, MTTM and related mean-based incident metrics. It defines a simple incident timeline (first impact, detection, mitigation, recovery) and uses public incident-status data from three internet companies plus a larger internal Google dataset. The author runs a Monte Carlo simulation of before-and-after samples, showing that even when a change is real, or when nothing changes at all, MTTR differences often appear by chance. The report closes by discussing why more incidents reduce variance and by exploring alternative analysis approaches. The page text provided is partial, so the later alternatives and conclusions are not included here.
